limitations: Diagnostic RTX 5000 results; not formal performance acceptance.
Before: CPU matrix generation with the existing GPU solve. After: CUDA matrix generation with the same GPU solve. This is not a CPU versus GPU solver comparison.

Full pipeline is continuously timed through public prepareAMS and amsPCG, including setup transfers, hierarchy/RHS upload and solution download. HDF5 reading and independent validation are excluded in both paths.
CPU reference solve is for numerical parity only; no CPU solve performance claim.
GPU setup memory is the exact maximum concurrently owned CUDA allocation bytes; pipeline memory is a live allocation delta, not whole-process peak.
Small case setup/solve stage sum regressed; no automatic backend fallback.
Only real FP64 lowest-order AMS cycles 1 and 7 covered; no complex, ICCG or HDiv-MMM certification.
The candidate was built from clean source. Published runtime and A100 were not modified.
rejected_prototypes: Direct triple-product accumulation was rejected: rounding differences changed the coarse factor.
Fused multiply/add was rejected. The accepted implementation preserves two-stage products with separate FP64 multiply/add rounding; all hierarchy arrays and factors match CPU bitwise.
